thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty PAGER FIRED: metering-ingest token-shard backpressure (shard-7) — severity: P1.
incident-bot: Pager: metering-collector-shard-7 — PD: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD12345 — please ack and triage.

pagerduty: Auto-escalation window set: 10m -> senior-sre if unacked.

Sara L: acked — I'm oncall and looking. Starting triage. :eyes:
Sara L: quick summary from PD: incoming producer queues are growing, consumer offsets stalled, token counts underreporting for a subset of customers. Potential invoice risk.

Raj K: joining. K8s logs and consumer metrics next. Any recent deploys to metering-collector-shard-7?
Sara L: no deploys in the last 2h. We started seeing spikes ~2056788500.

Sara L: running quick lag/offset check:
```
# kafka lag by partition (shard 7)
curl -s http://kafka-metrics.internal/lag?shard=7 | jq .max_lag
# expected < 1000, observed ~120000
```

Raj K: seeing high CPU on collector pods and socket backlog in logs. Sample from pod metering-collector-shard-7-0:
```
2025-11-03T06:23:45Z ERROR consumer read timeout: stalled for 30000ms, inflight=1024
2025-11-03T06:24:01Z WARN kv-cache miss spikes=0.7
```

Ana (billing): heads up — ops, if token undercounts persist some invoices will be short. We should prepare a manual invoice hold for affected customers until counts are reconciled.

Sara L: good call. Ana, please prepare the list of customers with >1% delta. We'll enable invoice hold flag for the billing pipeline.

Raj K: proposed mitigation steps:
1) scale metering-collector-shard-7 to 4 replicas
2) restart the consumer processes to clear stuck threads
3) if lag doesn't fall, re-route a subset of producers off shard-7 to shard-9 (capacity available)

Sara L: executing step 1 & 2 now.
```bash
kubectl -n metering scale deploy/metering-collector-shard-7 --replicas=4
kubectl -n metering rollout restart deploy/metering-collector-shard-7
```

oncall-bot: deploy rollout started for metering-collector-shard-7 (revision 42)
oncall-bot: alert: replica set scaling detected.

Sara L: restart completed. Observed quick memory drop and CPU normalize on 2 of 4 pods. Re-checking lag.

Sara L: lag decreased from ~120k -> ~18k in 6m. Not fixed but trending. Starting partial producer reroute for heavy customers to shard-9.
Raj K: applying routing change (gateway config):
```json
{ "route": "metering.prod/token_write", "match": "customer in (c123,c456)", "target_shard": 9 }
```

pagerduty: Note: escalation suppressed (acked within window).

Ana (billing): billing list ready. Creating manual invoice hold for customers with >1% delta (ticket BILL-908). Please confirm when you want holds applied.

Sara L: apply holds now for the highest risk customers (BILL-908 applied). We'll add a note for finance.

Mike T: I'm stepping in for handoff in ~20m (06:30 UTC). If anything changes escalate to me.

Raj K: after routing, lag down to 3.2k. Consumer error rates reduced. Network egress on shard-7 still slightly elevated but within thresholds.

Sara L: creating incident doc and timeline: INC-2056. Logging action items and owners.

Sara L: action items:
- Raj K: monitor and verify lag trend to 0 (owner)
- Mike T: post-handoff watch and ensure no regression (owner)
- Ana: continue holds & coordinate with finance (owner)
- DevEx: run postmortem on routing thresholds (TBD)

Sara L: current customer impact: delayed token ingestion for ~0.5% of active customers; some invoices for the window may undercount by up to 2-3% without holds. No data loss detected — messages are buffered.

Raj K: logs to review (examples):
```
kubectl -n metering logs metering-collector-shard-7-0 -c collector | grep "stalled" | tail -n 50
# sample: repeated stalls tied to long GC and socket backpressure
```

Sara L: monitoring — will update every 10m or on significant change. If lag goes above 20k again, re-open PD and escalate to senior-sre.

Ana (billing): confirmed hold applied for BILL-908. Finance notified. Thanks for the quick coord. :pray:

oncall-bot: incident status -> mitigated (partial) — reason: reroute + scale reduced backlog. Continue monitoring.

Mike T: taking over at 2056790200. I'm in. Following up on postmortem and any further remediation.

Sara L: thanks everyone. Leaving thread but will check in after handoff. :heavy_check_mark:
